During the limited [Model Hardware Standard (MHS)](https://www.anthropic.com/news/model-hardware-standard-research-preview) research preview (announced by Anthropic), I led Carnegie Mellon's work using MHS. The preview specification is provisional and model-agnostic; we used Claude as one agent.

An agent operated a liquid handler, plate reader, robotic arm, and cameras across three computers with incompatible interfaces. Serial-dilution dose-response experiments ran about three times faster than our prior workflow. The work is in the MHS announcement and in [*Nature* (24 September 2026)](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-02990-8); CMU SCS also posted on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:ugcPost:7498829877215842304/?actorCompanyId=28172194) and [X](https://x.com/SCSatCMU/status/2093063825171853484).

I wrote the MHS drivers for all three instruments and the orchestration layer. The agent ran the protocol, rejected a saturated curve, and reran with a lower maximum concentration ($R^2 > 0.98$), within device-declared safety bounds. Integration took about eight hours, compared with weeks of per-instrument integration.

Full write-up, photos, and video: [Safe closed-loop agentic dose-response experiments using the Model Hardware Standard](../posts/2026-08-27-mhs-preview.qmd).
